observations.text: The provider publishes OAuth server metadata at https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
The metadata lists PKCE code challenge methods: S256.
The metadata advertises a client registration endpoint (https://calendly.com/oauth/register), so apps may be creatable through an API.
observations.note: The agent did not register an app: that would create a real client on your behalf.

observations.text: Client authentication methods at the token endpoint: none.
The authorize endpoint sent an unauthenticated request to a sign-in page (calendly.com/app/login).
observations.how: GET https://calendly.com/oauth/authorize with a made-up client_id (oauth-guide-agent-probe), no login, redirects not followed
observations.note: Sign-in comes before any client check here, so the agent could not see how an unregistered client is treated.

observations.text: The token endpoint rejected an invalid test request with HTTP 401: "invalid_client: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method.".
observations.quote: invalid_client: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method. | WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Doorkeeper", error="invalid_client", error_description="Client aut
observations.how: POST https://calendly.com/oauth/token with a made-up authorization code and client (nothing is created or changed)
observations.note: So it validates the client and code before issuing anything. It asks for client authentication via the WWW-Authenticate header.

observations.text: A request to api.calendly.com with no token is rejected with HTTP 401.
observations.note: So API calls need an access token.

findings.text: Log in to Calendly or sign up for an account.
findings.quote: 1. Log in to Calendly, or sign up for a Calendly account.

findings.text: Open the Developer tools page.
findings.quote: 2. Open [Developer tools](https://calendly.com/app/developer). In Calendly, open the **Profile menu** and select **Developer**.

findings.text: Select Create OAuth app on the OAuth apps tab.
findings.quote: 3. On the **OAuth apps** tab, select **Create OAuth app**.

findings.text: Enter the app name, redirect URI, and environment type.
findings.quote:
4. Enter the app details:
   * **App name**: use letters, numbers, hyphens, and spaces only.
   * **Redirect URI**: the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
   * **Environment type**: select **Sandbox** for development and testing, or **Production** when your app is ready for real users.

findings.text: Select Next to proceed.
findings.quote: 5. Select **Next**.

findings.text: Select at least one scope for the app.
findings.quote: 6. Select the scopes that your app needs. Select at least one scope. Learn more about [scopes](/docs/authentication/scopes).

findings.text: Select Create to finish app creation.
findings.quote: 7. Select **Create**.

findings.text: Production apps must use https redirect URIs.
findings.quote: Production  | `https` URIs only

findings.text: Calendly recommends starting with a Sandbox app for development.
findings.quote: We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

findings.text: Authorization requests fail if they do not include a code challenge.
findings.quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the `S256` method. If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

findings.text: Client secrets and webhook keys cannot be viewed after the initial creation screen.
findings.quote: Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again. At this time, you also cannot view the client ID again in Developer tools.

findings.text: When your app initiates an OAuth flow, it should request the minimum set of scopes needed for your use cases.
